_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. The press-side records live in ~/printing-press/library/sophos-central/.printing-press-patches/ (ids prefixed sophos-).

handfixes.summary: the Sophos token endpoint reads client_id and client_secret only from the form body, never HTTP Basic
handfixes.why: id.sophos.com/api/v2/oauth2/token rejects the generated client's SetBasicAuth client-credentials request; credentials must ride in the application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Both mint paths (auth login and the client's automatic mint) carry the fix; without it every command fails INVALID_CLIENT.

handfixes.summary: key-based paging: pageFromKey cursor, next key read from pages.nextKey
handfixes.why: Sophos endpoint, alert, Live Discover result, audit-event and billing lists page with pageFromKey/pages.nextKey, not page numbers. The generated pager read the wrong cursor and either stopped after page one or repeated it. Sophos's partner getting-started guide: 'If the nextKey value is missing, you have reached the end of pages'.

handfixes.summary: a repeated or stuck cursor is reported as an incomplete listing, never returned as complete
handfixes.why: When the API repeats a cursor the generated walker either looped or returned a partial list as if it were complete; the fix turns both into an explicit incomplete-listing error so a fleet answer never silently drops machines.

asserts.contains: --all: pagination repeated cursor %q; listing is incomplete
stopped at %d pages with more available

handfixes.summary: sync treats a revisited cursor as a cycle and rows with no usable key as a failed (not complete) walk
handfixes.why: A cycled or stuck cursor and undecodable or keyless items used to let sync record a complete walk, after which --full pruned live rows that were merely unread. The walk is now marked incomplete so reconcile never deletes on partial data.

handfixes.summary: sync checkpoints and since-watermarks are keyed per tenant for tenant-scoped resources
handfixes.why: One local store holds every customer tenant (fleet refresh). A single checkpoint per resource meant tenant B resumed from tenant A's cursor and silently skipped rows; sophosSyncStateKey scopes each tenant-scoped resource's checkpoint to the active tenant.

handfixes.summary: a user --param that narrows the rows disables full-sync pruning
handfixes.why: sync --full prunes local rows the API no longer returns, but with a narrowing --param the API returns a subset by design, so pruning deleted every row outside the filter.

handfixes.summary: dependent (parent-keyed) sync drops parents stored for another tenant
handfixes.why: Parent-keyed sub-resources iterate the stored parent rows; with many tenants in one store, calling a parent ID under the wrong X-Tenant-ID returned 404s or, worse, another tenant's data.

asserts.contains: if parentRows, scopeErr = sophosScopeParentRows(db, dep, parentRows); scopeErr != nil {

handfixes.summary: local reads scope stored rows to the active tenant before paging
handfixes.why: fleet refresh puts every tenant's rows in one table; a local `endpoints list --tenant X` returned other tenants' machines without this filter, and paging before scoping returned short pages.

handfixes.summary: doctor, error hints and MCP tool text name the real Sophos credential setup (API Credentials menu, client ID + secret, --tenant)
handfixes.why: The generated hint pointed at a generic token flow; Sophos needs a service principal created under API Credentials, and a partner or organization credential must pick a tenant with --tenant.

handfixes.summary: platform tests accept that this spec owns the `whoami` command
handfixes.why: Sophos exposes GET /whoami/v1, so the API-generated `whoami` command replaces the framework one; the generated platform tests asserted the framework shape.

handfixes.summary: guide.md and SKILL.md document the tenant selector and leave the client secret as a placeholder
handfixes.why: The generated docs omitted SOPHOS_CENTRAL_TENANT_ID and showed a realistic-looking secret value in the env example; both are hand-fixed in the source docs that onboard re-vendors.

asserts.contains: Create an API credential in Sophos Central

handfixes.summary: MCP recipe intents refuse a flag-like value (leading '-') for a positional or string flag, e.g. contain's slug
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 recipe intents append agent-supplied values to argv; a value like '--yes' or '--base-url=...' became a flag (argv smuggling, see the fleet-wide finding on PR #317). rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue refuses it and string flags are passed as --name=value. Same fix as skills/acronis 'mcp-recipe-argv-not-flag-like'.

asserts.contains: if err := rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue("slug", input["slug"]); err != nil {

handfixes.summary: every request is routed by whoami: partner/organization calls go to the global host with X-Partner-ID / X-Organization-ID, tenant calls go to the tenant's regional apiHost with X-Tenant-ID, and the bearer token is only ever sent to a *.central.sophos.com host
handfixes.why: The generated client knows one base URL. Sophos Central splits its API across the global host (whoami, partner, organization) and a per-tenant regional host (endpoint, common, live-discover, xdr-query, account-health-check, siem) that each need a different ID header (developer.sophos.com/getting-started). sophos_routing.go installs a transport via the generated registerClientHook extension point, resolves the caller with GET /whoami/v1 (cached per credential), maps tenant -> apiHost, and rewrites host + headers. isSophosAPIHost refuses to send the token anywhere a cached or API-returned host would otherwise point. Novel file, so regen-merge keeps it; these asserts catch a reprint that drops the hook registration or the host guard.

handfixes.summary: the default local store and each tenant-scoped sync checkpoint are keyed per credential (base URL + client ID) and per tenant
handfixes.why: The generated store path keyed on the access token until one existed, so the first fleet refresh (no token yet) and every later command (token saved) used different database files, and two credentials could share one. sophosStoreScope pins the store to base URL + client ID; sophosSyncStateKey adds the tenant to each tenant-scoped checkpoint. Wired through the generated config.StoreScopeIdentity and resolveTenantID extension points.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token: neither the client's automatic mint nor `auth login` sends the client secret or writes credentials.toml during a preview
handfixes.why: A dry run is the preview the governance doc tells agents to run before every write. The generated client minted a token on the first request even under --dry-run, POSTing the client secret to id.sophos.com and persisting the token; `auth login --dry-run` minted through its own path. A preview must have no side effects.

handfixes.summary: a client secret read from SOPHOS_CENTRAL_CLIENT_SECRET is never written to credentials.toml, by the automatic mint or by `auth login`; only --client-secret is saved
handfixes.why: The fleet's issue #266 shape. SaveTokens wrote whatever secret it was handed, so the first API call (automatic mint) or `auth login` with only environment variables copied the secret from a secret manager into a plaintext file. MarkClientSecretFromEnv records the env source so configForSave keeps the file's existing value. Proven both directions by TestAuthLoginKeepsEnvSecretOffDisk (env case fails when the auth.go call is removed).

handfixes.summary: a response carrying a tamper protection password or a migration token is never cached, stored, exported or printed by tail, and the six operations that return one are not MCP-executable
handfixes.why: Sophos returns live credentials from exactly six operations (a scan of every 2xx response schema in the vendor spec for password/secret/token keys): GET and POST /endpoint/v1/endpoints/{id}/tamper-protection (password, previousPasswords) and GET/POST/PUT /endpoint/v1/migrations[/{id}] (token). The generated response cache wrote every GET body to disk, sync stored migration rows (resources table, FTS index and the typed migrations.token column), and the export and tail commands - both MCP tools - printed the token to any agent. Guards: the cache refuses a body with a secret key, every store write and the typed migrations writer drop secret keys, export and tail redact before printing (round 1 of this run caught `export migrations` leaking through MCP), and the MCP execute tool drops the six endpoint IDs. A human reads the tamper password with `endpoints get-tamper-protection` on the CLI.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press could mark response fields as x-sensitive in the spec and generate the cache, store, export/tail and MCP exclusions from that one declaration.

handfixes.summary: a client ID in SOPHOS_CENTRAL_CLIENT_ID that differs from the saved one is the credential in use: the saved secret and the token minted for the saved credential are never sent, and the environment credential's token stays in memory
handfixes.why: Round 1 adversarial review (2026-10-14) proved the generated precedence (saved config first, then environment) sent credential A's cached bearer token on a run configured with credential B, including from the MCP server (the CLI and MCP share the default data dir). With A an admin credential from `auth login` and B the read-only credential the docs tell owners to give an agent, an agent's writes ran with admin rights; after the token expired the client minted with A's saved ID and B's secret and failed with a misleading 401. AdoptEnvClientCredential runs in the client hook for both CLI and MCP, sophosClientPair (store scope and identity cache) uses the same rule, and `auth login` drops a saved secret that belongs to the client ID being replaced. TestEnvCredentialWinsOverSavedToken fails when the adopt call is neutralised.

asserts.contains: func (c *Config) KeepMintedTokenInMemory(accessToken string, expiry time.Time) bool {

handfixes.summary: SOPHOS_CENTRAL_TENANT_ID and the client pair are read through cliutil.EnvOverride in the hand-written routing and fleet code, so an unresolved MCPB ${user_config...} placeholder reads as unset
handfixes.why: Round 2 adversarial review proved an MCPB host that skips the optional tenant prompt leaves the literal ${user_config.sophos_central_tenant_id} in the environment; os.Getenv sent it as X-Tenant-ID and every fleet command failed with 'tenant ... is not managed by this partner credential'. The generated config already uses EnvOverride for exactly this; the hand-written routing did not. TestTenantPlaceholderIsUnset fails when configuredSophosTenant goes back to os.Getenv.

handfixes.summary: single-object GET commands return the whole object; a response path unwraps only a list wrapper (every other top-level key is paging metadata)
handfixes.why: The generator hands single-object GETs the first array property of the response schema as a response path. Round 1 adversarial review proved `alerts get` printed only allowedActions (the fleet triage next_command led nowhere), `tenants get` only products, and `endpoints get-tamper-protection` printed the INVALIDATED previous passwords under the key password while dropping the current password and enabled flag - a technician mid-incident would try a dead password. Also hit exploit-mitigation get-application-by-id, live-discover get-execution-summary, xdr get-query-run, web-control get-local-site-by-id and get-web-decryption-settings, software get-static-package and the three role get-by-id commands. applyEntityResponsePath is used only by the single-read resolver and passes list commands (isList) straight to the generated unwrap, so `licenses list` keeps printing rows (round 2 caught that regression); paginated list walkers keep applyResponsePath.

asserts.contains: func applyEntityResponsePath(data json.RawMessage, responsePath string, isList bool) json.RawMessage {

handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should only emit a response path for a single-object GET when the schema is a list wrapper (items plus paging keys).

handfixes.summary: every environment variable the binaries read is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md
handfixes.why: check_env_schema.py failed the first verify_all run: the generated manifest declared only the client ID and secret, while the binaries also read SOPHOS_CENTRAL_TENANT_ID, BASE_URL, TOKEN_URL, OAUTH_SCOPE, MCP_READ_ONLY, MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, USER_AGENT and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. A Claude Desktop install has no other way to set them. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on a re-onboard, so these asserts pin the declarations (issue #282 fleet shape). Optional values are blank in the copy-paste env blocks: a placeholder in an optional slot would be sent as a real value.

handfixes.summary: config.toml keeps the base URL, token URL and headers the file had: --tenant / SOPHOS_CENTRAL_TENANT_ID (applied as an X-Tenant-ID header) and SOPHOS_CENTRAL_BASE_URL / _TOKEN_URL apply to the current run only
handfixes.why: Round 3 adversarial review proved that installSophosRouting's X-Tenant-ID header was saved into config.toml [headers] on the next token save, so one `--tenant T1` run silently pinned every later CLI and MCP call (including writes such as isolation and policy changes) to T1 and skipped the router's tenantRequired refusal; `auth logout` did not clear it. The generated Load also saved env-supplied base and token URLs, so a later run posted the real client secret to an old token URL. persisted() now takes BaseURL, TokenURL and Headers from the file snapshot; no CLI command edits these on purpose (they are hand-edited in config.toml). TestTenantSelectionNotPersisted fails when the configForSave line is removed.

asserts.contains: out.BaseURL, out.TokenURL, out.Headers = c.fileConfig.BaseURL, c.fileConfig.TokenURL, c.fileConfig.Headers

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config.sophos_central_mcp_http_token} placeholder refuses to start instead of becoming the secret
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-14) found the generated requireHTTPCallerToken read SOPHOS_CENTRAL_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. The variable is declared as an optional MCPB user_config value, and a host that skips an optional prompt leaves the literal placeholder text in the environment; that text is public (it is in manifest.json), so anyone could authenticate to an HTTP-mode server started that way. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused fails when the read goes back to os.Getenv.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: the press main_mcp.go.tmpl should read the HTTP token through cliutil.EnvOverride for every connector.

handfixes.summary: export walks endpoints, alerts and audit events with pageFromKey / pages.nextKey, like sync and the list commands
handfixes.why: Codex review found resourceReadConfigs still declared these three key-paged Sophos resources as offset paging with no cursor parameter, so `export endpoints --limit 100` requested the same first page twice and an unlimited export repeated page one until the 100000-page guard. The sophos-key-paging hand-fix had covered sync and the list commands but not the export/tail resource table.

handfixes.summary: fleet refresh records when each resource was last refreshed; triage, health and gaps report synced_at and blind tenants from the resources they read
handfixes.why: The build pane's known gap, confirmed by Codex: one fleet_meta timestamp was stamped by any refresh, so `fleet refresh --resources health` made triage (endpoints, alerts) and gaps look freshly refreshed, and a tenant whose only refresh was health-only was not listed as blind. Each view now names the resources it depends on (triage: endpoints, alerts; health: health; gaps: health, endpoints, licenses); a missing resource gives synced_at null with a note and lists the tenant as not_refreshed. The triage 'new' flag uses the previous alerts refresh. TestPartialRefreshNotFreshForTriage fails when triage stops passing its resources.

handfixes.summary: fleet revenue compares billed seats with deployed endpoints per product; the customer-level billable_minus_deployed uses the largest single product line
handfixes.why: Codex review: the customer variance subtracted deployed endpoints from billable seats summed across every product, so ten machines with ten protection and ten encryption seats showed a false ten-seat discrepancy. One machine can consume several products.

handfixes.summary: fleet tamper bypasses the response cache so its plan reflects each tenant's current tamper protection setting
handfixes.why: Codex review: the global tamper setting came from the five-minute response cache, so turning tenant-wide tamper protection on in Sophos Central and rerunning `fleet tamper --yes` still reported global_off and skipped the tenant. The command's help already promised live reads.

handfixes.summary: doctor mints a token with the real credential and reports whether Sophos accepted it, instead of 'present, not verified'
handfixes.why: doctor is the command every doc tells an operator to run first. The generated version printed 'present, not verified' and left the operator to guess (issue #282 fleet shape). doctorProbeCredentials makes the token request and names the failure (for example INVALID_CLIENT) with the API Credentials menu path.

handfixes.summary: MCP shell-out tools refuse local-file source and destination flags (--home, --input, --notes-file, --playbook-file, --playbook-notes-file plus the generated output/receipt flags), and import is CLI-only
handfixes.why: Forwarded from a tool call, a local-path flag lets an agent read any file this account can reach (credentials.toml included) into the store, where playbook_list and sql hand it back, or write a file anywhere. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags walks the registered tool set by usage text so a newly generated local-path flag fails the test instead of shipping open. import needs --input, so it is hidden from MCP rather than a tool that always fails.

handfixes.summary: an explicit false for a boolean MCP argument is forwarded as --name=false
handfixes.why: cliArgsFromMCP dropped false booleans, so a default-true flag (tail --follow) could never be turned off from a tool call and tail ran forever inside the MCP server.

handfixes.summary: --client-profile is documented as inert on this connector and kept out of MCP tool schemas
handfixes.why: No tenant-gated client profile source is registered for Sophos Central, so the flag changes nothing; the generated help promised tenant gating it does not provide, and an agent could believe it had scoped itself. The help now says so and the MCP schema no longer offers it.

asserts.contains: Unused by this connector: no tenant-gated profile source is registered
